subject: Post-demo: ACME RAG eval & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Park <jenna@acme.com>, Tom Lee <tom.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-10T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: RAG eval recap + recommended next steps

Hi Jenna/Tom —

Thanks for your time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the ACME RAG evaluation:

What we heard:
- Primary goal: accurate, grounded responses for customer support KB (short FAQs + longer how-tos).
- Latency SLO: <400ms 95th for single-turn lookups; hopeful cost target ~ $0.002 / 1k tokens served.
- Data: ~500k docs (mix of product docs + transcripts); initial subset for eval = ~5k docs.

Recommended model/config (initial):
- Model family: Llama-3-70B (8k) quantized path for production (best tradeoff for grounding + cost).
- Eval model (for benchmarking): Llama-3-70B fp16 / Redwood-verified profile (we ran controlled tests; attached CSV).
- Reranker: cross-encoder reranker for precision-critical queries during eval (we can switch to bi-encoder + inexpensive reranker later if cost pressure).
- Retriever: sparse + hybrid ANN (BM25 seed + Faiss HNSW) with top_k retrieval = 50, rerank top_n = 10.

Metrics to track during eval (suggested):
- Grounding precision (percentage of answers with source citation + accurate span)
- Hallucination rate (manual sample)
- Retrieval recall@k and reranker precision@10
- Latency P50/P95 for retrieval + generation combined
- Token cost per query (batching simulated on typical traffic)

Attachments I shared here:
- acme_rag_benchmarks.csv (benchmarks from the sample dataset we ran)
- acme_prompt_set_v1.txt (initial prompt templates + eval prompts)
- SOW_draft_v1.pdf (outline for a 4-week eval engagement)

Proposed next steps:
1) ACME: Confirm you can share the 5k-doc eval subset by EOD Monday (secure link or S3 work).
2) Redwood: Spin up the eval harness and run overnight benchmarks on the subset; share preliminary numbers by Wed.
3) Technical deep-dive: schedule with your infra + data team to align retrieval/connectors (30–45m).
4) Pricing/timebox: If results look good, we finalize a short SOW for a 4-week pilot.

Can you confirm the dataset share timeline and whether the reranker recommendation (cross-encoder) is acceptable for the initial run?

Thanks — look forward to next steps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0123

Hi Jenna/Tom —

Thanks for the questions and the dataset timeline. A few quick notes from infra/serving side: 

- Llama-3-70B quant path: feasible on Redwood Dedicated for an eval-sized load, provided we use int8 quantization and our optimized kernels. We will provision a small cluster and isolate the run to keep costs predictable.
- Baselines: we'll run three configs in parallel during the first overnight run:
  * No reranker (top50 -> generate)
  * Bi-encoder reranker baseline (fast, cheaper)
  * Cross-encoder reranker (precision-focused)

- Logs & reproducibility: we'll export per-query retriever logs (doc ids, scores) and a sample of model outputs with grounding annotations (automated overlap score + manual sample tags). We will provide a Drive link with CSVs.
- Latency: expect combined P95 to be dominated by the cross-encoder reranker; if P95 goes above 700ms we will provide tuned configs (lower top_k, rerank top_n=5) to meet your SLO.

Next steps I'm taking this week:
- Vivek will provision the eval cluster once we get the S3 link.
- Marissa: I'll work with you to confirm SOW scope and cost estimates.

Vivek — please confirm when the cluster is up and provide expected cost burn estimate for a 48h test run so ACME can approve.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Serving | Redwood Inference
